        Here is the patch content:
        From b89414513c844a99569a5eb060522799fd8c185e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: MORITA Kazutaka <morita.kazutaka@lab.ntt.co.jp>
Date: Thu, 29 Aug 2013 09:54:32 +0900
Subject: [PATCH] dog: fix check of snapshot vdi

This fixes a bug introduced by the commit 996751b.

Signed-off-by: MORITA Kazutaka <morita.kazutaka@lab.ntt.co.jp>
Signed-off-by: Liu Yuan <namei.unix@gmail.com>
---
 dog/vdi.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/dog/vdi.c b/dog/vdi.c
index b0c2ea5a..46011408 100644
--- a/dog/vdi.c
+++ b/dog/vdi.c
@@ -1527,7 +1527,7 @@ int do_vdi_check(const struct sd_inode *inode)
 	for (int idx = 0; idx < max_idx; idx++) {
 		vid = inode->data_vdi_id[idx];
 		if (vid) {
-			oid = vid_to_data_oid(inode->vdi_id, idx);
+			oid = vid_to_data_oid(vid, idx);
 			queue_vdi_check_work(inode, oid, &done, wq);
 		} else {
 			done += SD_DATA_OBJ_SIZE;
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by an incorrect variable being passed to the function `vid_to_data_oid`. Instead of using `inode->vdi_id`, which likely refers to the VDI ID of the inode itself, the code should have used `vid`, which represents the VDI ID being processed in the loop. This mistake would lead to incorrect object IDs being generated for the snapshots, resulting in potential failures in the snapshot check process.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by an incorrect variable being passed to the function `vid_to_data_oid`. Instead of using `inode->vdi_id`, which likely refers to the VDI ID of the inode itself, the code should have used `vid`, which represents the VDI ID being processed in the loop. This mistake would lead to incorrect object IDs being generated for the snapshots, resulting in potential failures in the snapshot check process.
